verdict_note: From reading only (no build, no tests). The command layer is well made. Parameter decoding refuses unknown keys, wrong types, non-integers for integer fields and non-finite text. Every known hard bound of the 25-kind table equals pigment's validate at both edges (unit test table_hard_bounds_are_the_engines). The declared rows match the 14.9.7 tables (Fast Box Blur, Directional Blur, Radial Blur, Solarize, Mosaic, Minimax, Dust & Scratches). The STU-RAS-108 step derivation is exact. Reorder, toggle and remove each make one entry-only step that restores the previous entry bytes exactly. The harness-view -> interop-lrcat edge is acyclic and light. The defects are at the edges. F1 (high): effect.apply commits values inside the advertised hard range that pigment can never render. A box blur above MAX_BOX_KERNEL_TAPS (radius over about 1000 at the default 3 iterations, against an advertised hard_max of 30000), or any kernel kind on a layer holding values outside 0..1, makes every frame and export of the document refuse, while the command reports success. F2: the lead ruling 'a deleted layer's id is never minted again' holds for the 9000 block only. Adjustment layers (9300) and placed layers (9200) mint the first free counter after the entry prune, so they re-mint a deleted layer's id. F3: the 9eac2562 sentinel 'layer_id_space_exhausted-<salt>' does not fail safe everywhere. Vector and design-instance callers store the vector and text entries before the structure commit that then refuses, outside undo, and no caller outside layers.rs surfaces the typed code. F4: the DNG XMP keeps a caller packet's stale crs: crop when the Studio crop is full, and rewrites every managed crs: key only when a crop exists. F5: effect.* and adjustment.edit are entry-only steps. They are not document revisions and do not go through chronicle or a CommitPort, which contradicts the module doc. F6 and F7: the claims run ahead of the proof. The STU-FX-103/106 record and the STU-RAS-110 inputSchema bounds are not emitted. 'apply in place equals the adjustment layer' is shown only to within 1 of 8 bits on opaque pixels for two kinds, and its range rule differs from the composite's. F8 to F11 are low.

findings.certainty: READ (mechanism: validate vs cost/admit in pigment, render-cpu error mapping); not run
findings.severity: high (a successful command leaves the document unrenderable and unexportable until undo)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/raster_effects.rs:290-297 (box_blur hard radius 0..30000, iterations 1..50), :363 and :368 (surface_blur, bilateral_blur radius any u32), :720-751 (decode_kind: the only engine check is SmartFilterOp::check, i.e. FilterKernel::validate), :1017-1041 (effect_apply commits); crates/hsk-studio-pigment/src/filter_kernels.rs:179 (validate box 0..30000), :202-217 (cost: taps above MAX_BOX_KERNEL_TAPS is OverBudget 'inside their bounds, over the budget'), :287-297 (render_plane: admit(bounds) then check(p, UNIT) on every source sample); crates/hsk-studio-pigment/src/blur_math.rs:398 (MAX_BOX_KERNEL_TAPS = 6001); crates/hsk-studio-render-cpu/src/plan_sink/smart_filter.rs:111-115 (OverBudget -> BackendError::BudgetExceeded for the plan)
findings.what: The command checks only parameter validity, while pigment also refuses at render time. A box blur needs 2*floor(radius+0.5)*iterations+1 <= 6001 taps, so at the declared default of 3 iterations any radius above 1000 is over budget, and at 50 iterations any radius above 60. The spec record still advertises hard_max 30000, and STU-FX-105 says a value between soft and hard 'MUST succeed'. The FilterKernel render also refuses source planes with samples outside 0..1, but effect.apply never looks at the layer's range. Unbounded u32 radii of surface and bilateral blur reach the u64-window OverBudget of cost(). In each case the entry commits as one undo step and reports success. Every later composite of the document (canvas frame, PNG export, save previews) then refuses budget_exceeded or a filter error, because the stack is part of the document.
findings.scenario: (a) effect.apply {layer: art, filter_kind: box_blur, params: {radius_px: 2000}}: accepted (inside 0..30000, iterations default 3 gives 12001 taps). The next frame() is None and export.run / Viewer::export refuse budget_exceeded. Nothing names the filter as the cause. (b) The same with {radius_px: 127, iterations: 50} (both values inside the declared ranges, iterations outside soft only): 12701 taps, same failure. (c) effect.apply sharpen on a float layer holding 1.5 (a developed raw or a float TIFF layer): accepted, and the render refuses the unit check.
findings.fix: In effect_apply and effect_update, after decode_kind, run pigment's own admission over the layer's bounds: FilterKernel::cost(bounds, FilterLimits used by render-cpu), and LayerFilter's equivalent. Refuse budget_exceeded {filter_kind, needed, limit} before the commit. For FilterKernel kinds, refuse a layer whose samples leave 0..1 with a typed code (for example effect_source_range_unsupported), using place.rs sample_range over layer_rgba, or record it as a named cut. Do not change the advertised hard bounds: the budget depends on two parameters and the layer size, so it is an admission refusal, not a bound. State in effect.parameters that the box blur taps budget applies (a 'budget' note on the kind).
findings.test: viewer_raster_effects.rs: (a) box_blur radius 2000 refuses budget_exceeded with no undo step and the entry unchanged (refused helper), (b) radius 127 iterations 50 the same, (c) radius 1000 iterations 3 (6001 taps) is accepted and frame() renders. A float-layer fixture with values above 1 plus a kernel kind refuses typed and frame() still renders.

findings.certainty: READ (prune-then-mint order); which non-raster entries keep a deleted layer's id NOT_INSPECTED
findings.severity: medium (the lead-ordered failure class remains open in this lane's own minter; the V4-06 note says 'fixed')
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/place.rs:551 (create_layer_with_record: editable_entry(&doc) then mint_entry_layer_id(&doc, &entry, "9300")), :492-498 (editable_entry calls entry.prune(doc) first), :1315 (mint_placed_layer_id, block 9200), :1320-1337 (mint_entry_layer_id: the first counter n from 1 that doc layers, the pruned records or instances do not hold); lane file notes.v4_06 (9200 'fixed earlier', 9300 'fixed here')
findings.what: cb807859 and 9eac2562 make the 9000 block never mint an id twice (revision bits). The adjustment and placed blocks still take the first free counter. Their taken-set is computed after the prune, which has already dropped the deleted layer's raster_records row. So a deleted adjustment or placed layer's id is minted again by the next create. The raster row itself is not inherited, because it was pruned. But this is exactly the reuse the lead ruled out, and any record that another surface keys by that id and that the delete keeps then attaches to the new layer. Examples are node export settings (export.set_settings), chronicle property revisions, and vector or design records.
findings.scenario: adjustment.create {kind: invert} gives ...-7ede-9300-000000000001. viewer.delete_layer on it, then adjustment.create {kind: levels} gives ...-7ede-9300-000000000001 again. The same holds for asset.place, delete, asset.place (9200).
findings.fix: Mint both blocks with the revision scheme of layers.rs try_mint_layer_id: a shared helper over a block argument, with the typed layer_id_space_exhausted refusal. Keep the taken-set as a second guard. Correct notes.v4_06 for 9200 and 9300.
findings.test: viewer_raster_effects.rs: adjustment.create, delete, adjustment.create gives different ids. asset.place, delete, asset.place gives different ids. After save and reopen at the later revision, the same holds.

findings.certainty: READ (call order at each caller); whether a later vector-entry read refuses a sentinel-keyed live shape UNVERIFIED
findings.severity: medium (the 9eac2562 sentinel is not fail-safe everywhere, and the lead's typed-refusal condition is met only inside layers.rs)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/layers.rs:94-96 (mint_layer_id returns "layer_id_space_exhausted-<salt>"); view/vector.rs:1900-1913 (create_vector_layer: entry.live.push(StudioLiveShape {layer_id: id}) and store_entry at :1912, a direct non-undoable set_document_entry at :1888, BEFORE structure at :1913), :2196-2210 and :2696-2709 (store_entry before structure); view/design/instance.rs:452 (mint) and :1085-1092 (vector and text entries set directly, then structure); view/text.rs:719-723 (sentinel sliced into STXT-/STYS- ids, refused later as 'text_story: InvalidId story_id'); view/design/component.rs:481, :720 (restructure_and_entry, atomic, but Folio's code)
findings.what: Outside layers.rs the sentinel is not an SLYR id, so the layer creation eventually fails Folio's InvalidId check. In vector and instance paths, though, the vector and text entries are stored before that commit. These are direct document-entry writes ('Not undoable and not a revision', session.rs:3293). The refused creation therefore leaves behind an orphan path, a live shape keyed 'layer_id_space_exhausted-N' and, on instance redraw, text records, and all of them persist on save. No caller outside layers.rs reports layer_id_space_exhausted: a model sees folio invalid_id, a text_story or text_styles refusal, or 'no free layer id'. vector.rs free_layer_ids even returns the sentinels as Ok ids, because its taken() check passes them.
findings.scenario: A package whose document revision is 16777216 (crafted, or a long-lived document). A rectangle or ellipse tool with a live shape (create_vector_layer with live = Some) refuses at the structure commit, but the vector entry now holds the new path and a live shape keyed by the sentinel. A save writes it. A pathfinder or instance redraw does the same.
findings.fix: Delete the sentinel. Make mint_layer_id return Result<String, &'static str> (or use try_mint_layer_id) and propagate it with ? in all callers, before any entry write. The refusal's leading code is layer_id_space_exhausted. vector.rs free_layer_ids stops at the first Err. text.rs, vector.rs and design/*.rs are outside the owned paths, so they need the lead's PATH APPROVED and beyond_brief_paths lines.
findings.test: A fixture document at revision 2^24: the text tool, a live-shape rectangle, pathfinder, component create and instance redraw each refuse with the leading code layer_id_space_exhausted. The vector and text entries are byte-identical before and after, and no undo step is added.

findings.certainty: READ; Adobe crs: crop semantics (coordinate frame, CropAngle sign) UNVERIFIED (D5)
findings.severity: medium (a wrong crop in a shipped DNG; inconsistent rewriting of the caller's crs: keys)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/develop.rs:908-916 (dng_xmp_with_crop: `if !cropped ... return the caller packet unchanged`; with a crop, write_sidecar with the whole recipe), :1522 (cropped = state.extras.crop != NormalizedCrop::full()), :1550 (report 'xmp': 'crs_crop_keys'); crates/hsk-studio-interop-lrcat/src/xmp_sidecar.rs:1281-1318 (write_sidecar wants every managed crs: key, WhiteBalance, RetouchAreas, HasCrop); crates/hsk-studio-develop/src/dng_write.rs:15-24 ('the develop recipe as the XMP packet')
findings.what: (1) A full Studio crop writes nothing, so a caller packet that already holds crs:HasCrop=True with CropLeft and so on (for example a Lightroom sidecar handed to set_develop_dng_xmp) ships in the DNG unchanged. Readers then crop an image that Studio's recipe leaves uncropped. (2) With a crop, the codec rewrites every managed key that differs from the recipe: Exposure2012, WhiteBalance 'As Shot', the Enable* switches, RetouchAreas and so on. Toggling the crop therefore changes unrelated develop keys in the DNG, and the report calls it 'crs_crop_keys'. (3) A recipe the codec refuses (crs_recipe_invalid, crs_value_not_finite) is reported as xmp_invalid, 'the crs: codec refused the packet'. (4) Nothing reads the XMP back through lrcat read_sidecar. Studio's own DNG import does not read tag 700 (no read_sidecar caller in harness-view or harness-core), so reopening the exported DNG in Studio loses the crop and the recipe. That cut is not named.
findings.scenario: (a) set_develop_dng_xmp(packet with crs:HasCrop="True" crs:CropLeft="0.1"), Studio crop full, export DNG: the XMP still says cropped at 0.1. (b) A packet with crs:Exposure2012="+1.00" and a Studio exposure of 0: the uncropped export keeps +1.00, the cropped one writes +0.00.
findings.fix: Lead decision (Q4). Recommended: whenever a develop recipe exists, write it through write_sidecar into the caller packet or a fresh one, so a full crop writes HasCrop False. The codec's span edit keeps foreign properties. Report 'xmp': 'crs_recipe'. Map codec recipe refusals to their own code. Name in the cuts that Studio's DNG import does not read the crs: keys back.
findings.test: viewer_raster_effects.rs: (a) round trip: read_sidecar(xmp of the exported DNG, base recipe) returns crop == the Studio crop within 1e-6 and the crop keys in applied, with no crop losses. (b) Stale caller crop with a full Studio crop: the exported XMP has HasCrop False and the caller's keep:Note survives. (c) A caller's crs:Exposure2012 behaves the same with and without a crop.

findings.certainty: READ (harness.rs entry-only branch; session set_document_entry contract)
findings.severity: medium (host integration: effect edits bypass the commit path; a module doc claim is false)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/place.rs:526 (edit_raster_records: Run::set_tiles_and_entry(op, layer_id, None, ...)); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/harness.rs:1659-1690 (without tiles: session.set_document_entry plus a harness-only HistoryStep); crates/hsk-studio-session/src/session.rs:3293 ('Not undoable and not a revision'); raster_effects.rs:68-70 (doc: 'an edit commits through the session's chronicle provider after the checks here'); results carry revision_now() (place.rs:528), which is unchanged
findings.what: effect.apply, update, reorder, toggle and remove, and adjustment.edit, change rendered and saved content, yet they do not advance the document revision, pass no chronicle or CommitPort, and leave no receipt or idempotency key. adjustment.create (restructure_and_entry) and adjustment.apply (set_tiles) do go through chronicle. So the module doc's statement of the PromotionGate cut is wrong for six of the ten rows. The 'revision' each result reports is the previous one, so a model or host that tracks revision as its change or concurrency token cannot see these edits. Per the session descriptor, previews are written while they describe the revision being written, so set_previews(R), then effect.apply, then save writes previews without the filter. In a host bound to a CommitPort, the edits never reach the authority. Same pattern as embed_inner (the brief cites it), but now on the main effect surface.
findings.scenario: A host binds a CommitPort, a model runs effect.apply, the host syncs from receipts: the smart filter is missing at the authority. Or: set_previews at revision R, effect.apply (still R), save: the package preview shows the unfiltered layer.
findings.fix: Either commit effect and adjustment.edit edits as a revisioned step (a records step through chronicle, which needs a harness-core primitive: lead routing, Q3), or have the lead accept entry-only for this slice. Then correct raster_effects.rs:68-70 and the lane claim to say 'entry-only step: not a revision, no CommitPort', and name it in the cuts.
findings.test: If revisioned: after effect.apply the snapshot revision is higher by 1 and undo adds another revision. If accepted: a test pins that the revision is unchanged and that the stale-preview case drops the preview on save (or names it).

findings.certainty: READ against Master Spec v02.229 module 14
findings.severity: medium (the claims cover clauses that the output does not meet, and the cuts do not name them)
findings.where: raster_effects.rs:410-455 (param_spec_json emits hsk.studio.parameter_spec@1 with 'unknown' tokens and bound_classification); :249-254 and :251-252 (NOISE and PRESERVE options with discriminant 'unknown'); :465-532 (the contract check passes enumerations whenever options is non-empty); harness-core action/commands/photo.rs rows (params is an r() record with a text description, so it carries no schema bounds); lane file capabilities_done (STU-FX-104, STU-RAS-104..108/110/112); spec STU-FX-103 (14.9 l.12754), STU-FX-106 (l.12816), STU-RAS-109 (l.489), STU-RAS-110 (l.501), STU-RAS-035 (l.1348)
findings.what: (1) STU-FX-103 says every parameter of every StudioLiveFilter is one StudioEffectParameter (hsk.studio.effect_parameter@1) with display_name, a StudioParameterKind from STU-FX-112, null for absent bounds, bound_state (STU-FX-106: declared_both or declared_hard_only, ...), animatable, interpolable and options. None of these fields is emitted. The lane emits the STU-RAS-103 shape instead. The two clauses conflict: FX-106 declared_hard_only sets soft equal to hard, while RAS-104 forbids the copy. Choosing between them is a spec-owner question, not something an implementation should settle silently (Q2). (2) STU-RAS-110 requires the command's inputSchema to carry hard_* as schema bounds and soft, default, unit and step as annotations, but the effect.apply row has a free-text params record. (3) STU-RAS-109 requires a stable integer discriminant per member, yet distribution and preserve ship 'unknown'. Both are Studio's own enumerations, so Studio must declare them, and the contract check does not flag them. (4) STU-RAS-035 lists a 'built-in mask' for the adjustment layer, but adjustment.create creates none and the cuts name only filter masks.
findings.scenario: A model reads effect.parameters for add_noise and gets distribution options without discriminants. A client that validates against help --json inputSchema sees no bounds for box_blur.radius_px.
findings.fix: Narrow the claims to what is emitted, and add to the cuts: the FX-103 record and bound_state, the RAS-110 inputSchema annotations, and the adjustment layer's built-in mask (unless an existing layer-mask command covers adjustment layers: cite it). Declare Studio discriminants for SmartNoiseDistribution and SmartMorphPreserve (contiguous from 1). Extend parameter_contract_findings with discriminant_missing for enumerations.
findings.test: the_contract_check_finds_each_defect_class gains an enumeration with an 'unknown' discriminant that must be found. The shipped table then shows findings == [] with the declared discriminants.

findings.certainty: READ (render.rs records envelope at unit range; composite_adjustment_in); straight vs premultiplied backdrop NOT_INSPECTED
findings.severity: medium (the equality is asserted beyond its proof; the range rule differs from the layer form)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness/tests/viewer_raster_effects.rs:263-271 (close(): every 8-bit channel within 1; one opaque 16x16 layer; invert and levels only); place.rs:598 (extended = the LAYER's own measured range) vs crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/render.rs:410-414 (a document with raster records renders with the envelope's default output stage, unit range) and crates/hsk-studio-render-cpu/src/plan_sink/extended.rs:1009 (composite_adjustment_in(output.sample_range, ...)); pigment adjust_math.rs:778-790 (apply_in Extended: only Exposure, others Unsupported)
findings.what: The in-place form chooses Unit or Extended from the layer's pixels, while the adjustment layer uses the plan's output range, which is unit in the viewer whenever raster records exist. On a layer with values outside 0..1, adjustment.apply refuses adjust_unsupported for 19 of the 20 kinds, yet the same adjustment as a layer renders. For exposure, the in-place result is unclamped while the layer form clamps. Either way, the frames are not equal and STU-RAS-035's 'every kind ... as an explicit destructive apply-in-place command' fails for such layers. The proof is also weaker than the claim. It allows plus or minus 1 per 8-bit channel (a systematic one-level bias passes). It has no partial-alpha texels, though composite_adjustment_in works on the backdrop colour and keeps alpha, and whether that backdrop is straight is not checked. It covers 2 of 20 kinds and compares the 8-bit display frame rather than float values.
findings.scenario: A float TIFF layer with a highlight at 1.4: adjustment.create {kind: levels} over it renders, while adjustment.apply {layer, adjustment: levels} refuses adjust_unsupported.
findings.fix: Use the composite's rule: the output range of the plan the viewer renders (unit for a records envelope), so the in-place result equals the layer form. Or name the float-layer case as a cut and weaken the doc claim to 'unit-range layers'.
findings.test: Compare float values (render_linear_with_records, or the tiles' f32 values against the composite of the layer form) for exact equality or a stated ulp bound. Use a fixture with partial-alpha texels and run every kind with a valid record (a parameterised list). Add one float-range layer case pinned to the chosen rule.

findings.severity: low (V4-02 aggregate: memory amplification on large liquify entries)
findings.where: raster_effects.rs:1053-1063 (effect_update: kind_params serializes the whole entry to Value, then merged, decode_kind, check_param clones, Folio decode, probe clone, pigment from_record), :695-705 (the mesh cap counts list length only), :1004-1013 (effect.read returns every entry's params in full)
findings.what: A liquify entry may hold MAX_LIQUIFY_VERTICES = 2^22 displacement pairs. An opacity-only effect.update converts that mesh to serde_json Values and copies it several times. effect.read returns it whole through the JSONL loop, with no aggregate byte budget and no summary mode.
findings.scenario: photo.liquify with a large mesh, then effect.update {opacity: 50} and effect.read: peak memory runs to several copies of the mesh as JSON Values, and the read reply runs to hundreds of MB.
findings.fix: In effect.update, skip the re-decode when params is absent (opacity only). In effect.read, summarise mesh params (cols, rows, spacing, counts) unless asked for in full, or cap the reply bytes with a typed refusal.
findings.test: A 2^20-vertex mesh entry: an opacity-only update does not re-decode the mesh (a counter, or a size-bound reply), and effect.read's reply stays under a stated byte bound.

answers.parameter_validation: Complete for types and known bounds. Unknown keys refuse parameter_unknown; wrong types and 3.0 for an integer refuse parameter_invalid. JSON cannot carry NaN or infinities, so params given as text must parse as JSON, and opacity given as text ('NaN', 'inf', '1e309') is refused as non-finite. Every known hard bound equals pigment's at both edges (unit test table_hard_bounds_are_the_engines). Unknown bounds stay unbounded except the f32 magnitude limit. The declared rows match the spec tables. The gaps are F1 (admission budget and source range), F8 (f32 rounding) and F10 (declared centre default, the dust unit, the opacity code).
answers.undo_exactness: Exact. edit_raster_records makes one entry-only HistoryStep whose restore holds the previous entry bytes, or None when there was no entry, and undo writes them back byte for byte (harness.rs:1663, :1688). The step also carries the editable_entry prune of other deleted layers' stale rows and the canonical re-serialisation; undo restores both. adjustment.create is one restructure_and_entry step and adjustment.apply one tile step. Tests: remove undo and redo, and adjustment.apply undo. Reorder and toggle undo are not tested directly; they share the same mechanism.
answers.apply_in_place_equals_layer: Asserted, not proven pixel-exact: within 1 of 8 bits, on opaque pixels, for two kinds, on a lone layer. The range rule differs from the composite (F7).
answers.xmp_crop: Keys CropTop, CropLeft, CropBottom, CropRight (6 decimals, 0..1), CropAngle (signed, 2 decimals, -45..45, the same range develop validates, recipe.rs:129) and HasCrop, written by the lrcat codec only (no second crs: writer: confirmed). Foreign properties are kept (test: keep:Note). With a crop, every managed crs: key is rewritten to the recipe, and without one nothing is written, including a stale caller crop (F4). Flips have no key (named). There is no read round trip through read_sidecar (F4). Adobe coordinate frame and CropAngle sign: UNVERIFIED (D5). develop refuses crop.orientation other than 1, so the orientation mapping is not exercised.
